title: Capacity Sizing Framework and Quarter-by-Quarter Rollout Plan for Dedicated Autoscale
creator: Elena Marquez
description: Purpose: define a repeatable, quarter-by-quarter capacity sizing framework and an operational rollout plan that ties Dedicated customer reservations, autoscale policies, and financial hedging together. This ticket captures the PM-level decisions, acceptance criteria, and cross-functional tasks required to ship a Q2 pilot and a staged rollout in Q3. Key outcomes: a sizing band model (small/medium/large clusters), demand-window simulation tooling, contract cadence recommendations, and an ops runbook for fast-fail scale-ups and fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Sizing model v1 documented with discrete bands and compute-to-throughput mapping
Demand simulation harness can run representative traffic for top 20 customers and produce expected CPU/GPU and KV-cache utilization curves
Autoscale policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) defined with SLO guardrails and cost trade-offs
Billing & reservation guidance drafted for Sales and Finance, with example customer quotes for 3 sizing bands
Pilot plan and success metrics for a limited customer cohort are approved by PM, Eng, and Sales
Operational runbook including canary steps, rollback conditions, and incident playbook is in the Console docs
tasks: Run historical usage analysis for top 50 dedicated customers and extract peak-window distributions
Build demand-window simulator that can replay token/time distributions and produce latency/cost forecasts
Collaborate with Runtime Eng to map sizing bands to GPU types and batch throughput
Define three autoscale policy templates and encode them into policy spec for Dedicated control plane
Draft finance guidance: reservation hedging, early-termination rules, and billing proration examples
Create pilot customer list and contact owner (Sales) to coordinate a Q2 pilot
Write Console UI copy and selection defaults for sizing bands and autoscale templates
Run 2 synthetic stress tests in staging with canary quotas and capture SLO/latency regressions
Prepare a rollout timeline and internal communications (KB, release notes, training)
milestones: 2026-06-30: Documentation and GA rollout plan finalized
metrics: Cost metric: avg cost per 1M tokens for each sizing band (target defined by FinOps)
Latency SLO: p95 generation latency for pilot customers remains within SLA
Utilization: target sustained GPU utilization bands per sizing tier
Forecast accuracy: simulator 90th percentile error <20% vs observed in pilot
risks: Simulator underfitting: synthetic load may not represent edge-case burst patterns
Reservation mismatch: customers choose wrong sizing band leading to over/under provision
Billing complexity: proration and bursting could create invoicing confusion
Operational: fast-fail scale path may introduce transient latency spikes if not properly throttled
Cross-team bandwidth: Eng priorities on runtime improvements may slip and delay pilot
notes: Differentiators: emphasize predictable economics and guardrails rather than fully automated aggressive autoscaling out of the gate. For Q2 we aim to ship conservative templates and a simulation-driven sizing guide that Sales can use. Follow-up work for Q3 will focus on contract automation, dynamic hedging, and expanded templates for bursty workloads. Keep pilot limited to customers with well-understood traffic shapes.
